name: Solar farm (utility / community)
summary: Ground-mount single-axis-tracking PV priced per MWdc. Cost is dominated by modules, trackers/racking and electrical BOS. Scale economies are strong: LBNL finds projects over 250 MWac cost about 60% less per watt than projects under 20 MWac, so community-scale (1–20 MWac) projects sit at the high end. Data quality is high: an itemized Sargent & Lundy/EIA estimate, the DOE/NREL bottom-up benchmark and LBNL empirical plant data all agree within about 15%.

typicalSize.method: Mid = DOE/NREL representative utility-scale system of 100 MWdc (e3); EIA reference case is 195 MWdc (e1). Low 5 MWdc = typical community-solar scale; high 250 MWdc = large utility-scale (LBNL size bin >250 MWac, e4).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: EIA/S&L case 16 assumes 1,000 acres for 195 MWdc (150 MWac) = 0.195 MWdc/acre (about 5.1 acres per MWdc). Range ±25% for terrain, setbacks, tracker vs fixed tilt and ground-coverage ratio.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Unstaffed plant; only a few gravel spaces at the O&M/substation area (≈5 spaces per 100 MW at most).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard cost = EPC price per MWdc. e1 EIA/S&L EPC subtotal $211.085M / 195 MWdc = $1.08M/MWdc (2023$, includes substation, EPC indirects, fee and 5% EPC contingency; excludes owner's costs and interconnection). e2 LBNL 2023 capacity-weighted total installed cost $1.08/Wdc × 0.90 EPC share (EPC/total = 0.937 in e1) ≈ $0.97M. e3 DOE/NREL 2025Q1 PV-only modeled market price $1.12/Wdc (2024$) includes developer overhead/profit/interconnection; × 0.90 ≈ $1.01M. e4 LBNL 2024 average $1.22/Wdc × 0.90 ≈ $1.10M. Mid = rounded average of the four (~$1.04M) → $1.05M in 2024$ (evidence spans 2023–2024, gap ≤ 1 yr). Low = LBNL >250 MWac bin $1.38/Wac ÷ 1.32 DC/AC × 0.90 ≈ $0.94M, rounded down to $0.90M. High = LBNL <20 MWac bin $2.19/Wac ÷ 1.32 × 0.90 ≈ $1.49M → $1.5M (community-scale).

scope.notes: EPC price incl. modules, inverters, trackers, DC/AC collection, on-site project substation/main power transformer, civil (grading, access roads, fencing), EPC indirects, fee and EPC contingency. Excludes land/lease, developer/owner soft costs, interconnection/transmission line and network upgrades, financing.

systemSplit.method: From EIA/S&L Case 16 EPC components (total $211.085M): 48 = module supply 72.15 + inverter supply 10.395 + 65% of racking/tracker/BOP supply (44.85) + 70% of installation labor (26.325) = 130.125; 26 = 35% of racking/tracker/BOP supply (DC/AC cabling, combiners) + 30% of labor = 23.595; 33 = main power transformer & substation 10.5; 25 = SCADA 0.915; civil/structural subcontract 13.65 split 31 earthwork 50% / 32 roads & fencing 35% / 03 foundations 15%; 01 = indirects 12.675 + EPC fee 9.573 + EPC contingency 10.052 = 32.3. The 65/35 and 70/30 splits of tracker/BOP and labor are assumptions (verify).

lineItems.name: PV module supply (bifacial mono)

cost.method: e1 module supply $72.15M / 195 MWdc = $370k/MWdc. Range ±20% for tariff/AD-CVD exposure and domestic-content modules.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; most volatile line (tariffs, FEOC/domestic-content rules).

lineItems.name: Project substation & main power transformer

cost.method: e1 'Main Power Transformer and Substation' $10.5M for 150 MWac. Low/high ±~40% for voltage class and size; small community projects that tie in at distribution voltage may need only a recloser/pad transformer (well below low).

lineItems.notes: Inside the baseline per-MW rate for a ~100–200 MW project.

lineItems.name: Generator tie / transmission line to POI

cost.method: e1 transmission line cost $2,412,000 per mile ÷ 5,280 LF = $457/LF; default 1 mile per e1. Range assumed ±35% for voltage and terrain.

lineItems.notes: Owner's cost in EIA; outside the property line — excluded from hard-cost baseline.

lineItems.name: Utility network upgrade allocation

cost.method: Placeholder allowance: highly site- and queue-specific (from $0 to several hundred $k/MW). Mid $50k/MWdc ≈ 5% of hard cost. Verify with the interconnection study (facilities study / LGIA).

lineItems.notes: Set from the interconnection agreement when available.

lineItems.name: Co-located battery storage adder (≈2.4 MWh per MWdc)

cost.method: e3 DOE/NREL 2025Q1 utility PV+ESS MMP $1.81/Wdc minus PV-only $1.12/Wdc = $0.69/Wdc for a 240 MWh ESS on 100 MWdc. Range ±20%. Use the battery-storage type for a standalone estimate.

pctOfHard.method: e1 owner's costs (development, studies, permitting, legal, owner's PM/engineering) = 5% of EPC plus interconnection and owner contingency = 6.8% of EPC total. Low 6% = that. Mid 10% adds developer margin/financing fees implied by the ~10% gap between EPC and total installed cost (e1, e2–e4). High 18% for community solar with subscriber acquisition and small-project fixed development costs.

softCosts.notes: Excludes interconnection network upgrades (line item) and land lease (operating cost).

design.method: Mature, repetitive technology; design contingency mainly geotech (pile refusal) and layout changes.

hard.method: e1 applies a 5% EPC contingency on EPC costs; used as the mid owner hard contingency. High for tariff-exposed module procurement.

soft.method: e1 owner's contingency = 10% of owner's costs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Total installed cost (hard + soft, excl. land): LBNL >250 MWac ≈ $1.05/Wdc down to ~$0.85 for the cheapest plants; <20 MWac ≈ $1.66/Wdc, with small community projects up to ~$2.0/Wdc.

source.title: Capital Cost and Performance Characteristic Estimates for Utility Scale Electric Power Generating Technologies (Sargent & Lundy for EIA), Case 16 Solar PV with Single-Axis Tracking, 150 MWAC
source.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration / Sargent & Lundy

evidence.quote: Table 16-1 — Case 16 Capital Cost Estimate (2023 $): EPC Subtotal $211,085,000; Total Capital Cost $225,348,000; $/kW net 1,502; 'This case uses 195 MWDC of monocrystalline ... bifacial modules'; Estimated Land Requirement 1000 acres.
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = EPC subtotal / 195 MWdc. EPC includes modules, inverters, tracker/BOP, MPT & substation, labor, SCADA, civil, indirects, 5% fee, 5% contingency. Owner's costs ($14.263M: services, 1-mile interconnection, contingency) excluded. Total capital cost = $1.156M/MWdc.

evidence.quote: Relative to 2022, capacity-weighted averages decreased by 8% to $1.43/WAC (or $1.08/WDC). Costs, based on a 7.1 GWAC sample of 76 plants completed in 2023
evidence.scopeNotes: Empirical total installed project cost (EPC + developer/owner costs, typically incl. interconnection), plants >5 MWac. Converted to hard cost with ×0.90 in method.

source.title: Solar Photovoltaic System Cost Benchmarks (2025Q1 benchmarks)
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Solar Energy Technologies Office (NREL modeling)

evidence.quote: The representative utility-scale PV system for 2025 has a rating of 100 MWdc. Table 2 (PV-only): MSP $1.07/Wdc; MMP $1.12/Wdc. Table 1 (PV + 240 MWh ESS): MMP $1.81/Wdc. All dollar values are inflation-adjusted to 2024 U.S. dollars.
evidence.scopeNotes: Modeled market price includes hardware, labor, EPC and developer overhead, permitting/interconnection and profit — i.e., closer to total installed cost than EPC hard cost.

source.title: Cost of Utility-Scale Solar: LCOE, PPAs, and Storage (summarizing LBNL U.S. Utility-Scale Solar, 2025 Data Update slides)
source.publisher: LegalClarity (secondary, citing Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)
